translation: (Dialogue) Daughter-in-law: Mother-in-law... O mother-in-law... have your eyes cooled down at last? Mother-in-law: Oh, may your eyes burn... what's happened, why are you talking like that?

Song: Daughter-in-law: Why do your eyes burn so much at the sight of me, O mother-in-law, why, O mother-in-law... why do you set fire to my married life, O mother-in-law? Mother-in-law: May fire fall on your suspicions, you daughter-in-law, you wily daughter-in-law... why do you flare up the moment you see me, daughter-in-law? Daughter-in-law: You told made-up tales and got me beaten, mother-in-law, you got your son to beat me, mother-in-law — may your son's hands break — look at these bruises, mother-in-law.

(Dialogue) Mother-in-law: Hey, Yadagiri... are you watching what your wife is up to? Daughter-in-law: So what if he watches... am I afraid of anything? Mother-in-law: Oh mother... how shameless you've become... may earth fall on your house! Daughter-in-law: Let it fall... may earth fall on your own house... may dust fall on it! Mother-in-law: You say earth should fall on my house... may boils break out on your hands!

Song: Daughter-in-law: When we bring plenty and feed you, you can't digest what you eat, and when you talk back, will he just keep quiet and not hit you? (When you talk back, will he just keep quiet and not hit you?) Mother-in-law: Mother-in-law, may the plague take you — are you laughing? Are you throwing away a daughter like me? (Are you throwing away a daughter like me?) Hey, may blisters break out in your mouth, why did you say such things, you quarrelsome daughter-in-law... are you throwing away a mother like me?

(Dialogue) Daughter-in-law: Are you listening, you bedbug-bitten man... to your mother's words! Mother-in-law: Are you listening, O Shanthakka... just look at her two-faced talk! Daughter-in-law: Oh ho... here comes my mother-in-law... acting the innocent, as if she's done nothing... Mother-in-law: What have I done... may a corpse be carried out of your house! Daughter-in-law: This whole village knows what kind of woman you are! Mother-in-law: What... what does anyone know about me?

Song: Daughter-in-law: If you were a sensible mother-in-law, wouldn't you set us up in a separate home? If you divided and gave us what's ours, wouldn't that be the respectable thing? (If you divided and gave us what's ours, wouldn't that be the respectable thing?) Mother-in-law: I won't give you so much as a broken cowrie — go off and make your own living. If you start this kind of racket, I'll beat you with the broom. (If you start this kind of racket, I'll beat you with the broom.) Weren't you too once a daughter-in-law to a mother-in-law? Mother-in-law, have you forgotten... didn't you egg on your innocent father-in-law and split off on your own?

(Dialogue) Daughter-in-law: I'm not like you... I looked after my in-laws well... the grace on my foot isn't even on your face! Mother-in-law: Ah... it shows, it shows... what fine words you have... what will you do... what will you do, coming at me again and again? Daughter-in-law: Me, coming at you? You may be an old woman, but you're prancing about like a young girl! Mother-in-law: Me... me a young girl... are you seeing this, sir — may her grave cave in!

Song: Daughter-in-law: May your mouth be struck dumb, why do you shout in the open street? What have you ever brought and given me, why do you put on such airs? (What have you ever brought and given me, why do you put on such airs?) Mother-in-law: What did you ever have to begin with, that you're so pleased with yourself, mother-in-law? Isn't all this property your own in-laws'? (Isn't all this property your own in-laws'?) You answer back at every word, you daughter-in-law, you wily daughter-in-law... you've snagged on me like a thorn bush — may earth fall in your eyes!

(Dialogue) Daughter-in-law: Yes, yes, I'm the thorn bush... may your whole clan be ruined... my people hung me out on some thorn bush from who knows where! Mother-in-law: Yes you are... I married you to my son thinking you were a lovely, pretty girl... may crows peck out your eyes! Daughter-in-law: You want crows to peck at me... may kites pluck the hair off your head! Mother-in-law: Oh my... look how shameless she's become... may termites breed on her hands! Daughter-in-law: You want termites on my hands... may sores break out on your hands... may your leg break! Mother-in-law: What... you dog-faced woman... you say whatever you please to me? Daughter-in-law: Hey, come on... you keep coming at me... will you hit me? Go on, hit me... come on, hit... just try one blow! Mother-in-law: And if I hit you, what will you do... just wait right there!
summaryEn:
This is a comic quarrel between an atta (mother-in-law) and her kodalu (daughter-in-law), performed as alternating spoken dialogue and sung verses. The two women trade accusations and increasingly inventive curses: may earth fall on your house, may crows peck your eyes, may kites pluck your hair, may termites breed on your hands. Behind the insults lie familiar tensions of the joint family. The daughter-in-law complains that her mother-in-law's tales got her beaten by her husband Yadagiri, and she demands that the family property be divided so the young couple can set up a separate household. The mother-in-law refuses to give up even a broken cowrie and threatens her with a broom, and the daughter-in-law reminds her that she was once a daughter-in-law herself who broke away from her own in-laws.

Both women appeal to onlookers — the husband and a neighbour, Shanthakka — which makes the song feel like a village street drama. Its humour comes from the rapid back-and-forth, the echoed lines and the rich Telangana dialect of everyday scolding. In a few places the speaker labels in the source seem to sit on the wrong lines, so the reader should follow the sense of the argument.
summaryTe:
ఈ పాట అత్తా కోడళ్ల మధ్య జరిగే హాస్యభరితమైన గొడవ. మాటల డైలాగులు, పాట చరణాలు మార్చి మార్చి వస్తూ ఒక వీధి నాటకంలా సాగుతుంది. ఇద్దరూ ఒకరిపై ఒకరు నిందలు వేసుకుంటూ ‘నీ ఇంట్ల మన్నువడ’, ‘నీ కండ్లల్ల కాకులు పొడవ’, ‘నీ నెత్తెంట్రుకలు గద్దలు పీక’, ‘చేతులకు చెదలు పుట్ట’ వంటి తెలంగాణ పల్లె తిట్లను పోటీపడి విసురుకుంటారు. ఈ తిట్ల వెనుక ఉమ్మడి కుటుంబంలోని అసలు సమస్యలు కనిపిస్తాయి. అత్త చెప్పిన లేనిపోని మాటల వల్ల భర్త యాదగిరి తనను కొట్టాడని కోడలు బాధపడుతుంది, ఆస్తి పంచి తమను వేరు కాపురం పెట్టమని అడుగుతుంది. అత్త చిల్లిగవ్వ కూడా ఇవ్వనని, చీపురుతో కొడతానని బెదిరిస్తే, నువ్వు కూడా ఒకప్పుడు కోడలివేనని, మామను ఎగదోసి వేరుపడలేదా అని కోడలు గుర్తుచేస్తుంది.

ఇద్దరూ భర్తను, పొరుగింటి శాంతక్కను సాక్షులుగా పిలవడం వల్ల పాట ఊరంతా చూసే గొడవలా అనిపిస్తుంది. వేగంగా సాగే మాటల యుద్ధం, పునరావృతమయ్యే పాదాలు, రోజువారీ తెలంగాణ యాస ఈ పాటకు హాస్యాన్ని ఇస్తాయి. మూలంలో కొన్ని చోట్ల ఎవరు మాట్లాడుతున్నారో చూపే పేర్లు తప్పు పాదాల దగ్గర ఉన్నట్టు కనిపిస్తాయి, కాబట్టి వాదన అర్థాన్ని బట్టి చదువుకోవాలి.
